item.title: Integrating Leadership and Green Human Resource Management for Sustainable and Thriving Workplaces
item.content:encoded:
Azadeh Shafaei, Edith Cowan University

Mehran Nejati, Edith Cowan University

This special issue examines how leadership and green human resource management integrate to create sustainable and thriving workplaces. As organisations face environmental and social pressures, they must embed sustainability into HR systems while supporting employee wellbeing. The issue seeks research on how leadership approaches influence GHRM design, implementation, and effectiveness, and their impact on employee and organisational outcomes.

Beyond celebrating sustainability initiatives, the special issue encourages critical examination of their challenges and downsides. Green practices can intensify work demands, create role ambiguity, generate cynicism when perceived as inauthentic greenwashing, or trigger stress and fatigue. Balanced analysis of both benefits and unintended consequences is welcomed.

Contributions are invited exploring leadership-driven GHRM mechanisms, contextual factors determining effectiveness, and employee experiences including wellbeing, engagement, inclusion, and psychological safety, alongside critical perspectives on paradoxes and negative aspects of sustainability-focused workplace initiatives.

  • Leadership and Green Human Resource Management (GHRM)

  • Authenticity, Greenwashing, and Employee Responses to Sustainability Initiatives
  • The Bright and Dark Sides of Green Human Resource Management
  • Multi-Level, Cross-Cultural, and Digital Perspectives on Sustainable Workplaces
